mainTopic: The priestly gifts from a doubtful firstborn, the רבי טרפון / רבי עקיבא dispute over a doubtful firstborn lamb, and a new משנה on two ewes giving birth.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question on רבי אלעזר. The סיפא of the משנה seems to already say that רבי יוסי exempts the priestly gifts because the כהן holds the animal's replacement (חליפין ביד כהן). The גמרא answers that without רבי אלעזר, we might have thought רבי יוסי was only arguing on רבי מאיר's terms. Next, רב פפא says everyone agrees that a ספק מעשר animal is exempt from the gifts. The גמרא shows why that statement is needed even for רבי מאיר. The גמרא then explains the argument between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא when one of the lambs dies. רבי טרפון retracted his earlier view, and רבי חייא gives two parables, a shepherd and a homeowner. רבא explains that both sides agree on the parables. They argue only about the owner's courtyard when the shepherd is a כהן. A new משנה then lays out cases of two ewes giving birth, some certain and some doubtful. The גמרא begins explaining why each case was needed, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה's later clause already shows that the reason is the replacement being in the כהן's hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the later clause (סיפא) of the משנה, in which רבי יוסי exempts any animal whose replacement is with the כהן. From this it infers that רבי אלעזר's explanation is already obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any animal whose replacement is in the hand of the כהן is exempt from the priestly gifts, and רבי מאיר obligates. So if the replacement is in the כהן's hand, yes, it is exempt. If the replacement is not in the כהן's hand, no, it is not exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge against רבי אלעזר. It quotes the סיפא of the משנה, which seems to already say exactly what he said, so his statement looks unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording 'כל שחליפיו ביד כהן' ties the exemption directly to the replacement being with the כהן. The גמרא reads it precisely: with a replacement there is an exemption, without one there is none. That is exactly רבי אלעזר's point, so why did he need to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: Replacement or exchange; here, the animal the כהן 'holds' in place of the doubtful one
The priestly gifts from a slaughtered animal: foreleg, cheeks, and maw
Exempt
Obligates; holds that one must give
Yes / no; a formula for drawing a precise inference from a text

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not a new ruling. It is the end of a challenge that began on the previous amud: the claim that רבי אלעזר's statement is 'obvious' (פשיטא) because of this clause of the משנה.

phrases.english: Any animal whose replacement is in the hand of the priest
phrases.notes: Quoted from the סיפא of the משנה, giving רבי יוסי's view

phrases.english: is exempt from the priestly gifts,
and Rabbi Meir obligates.
Replacement in the priest's hand: yes, exempt,
phrases.notes: The גמרא's inference from the wording

phrases.english: no replacement in the priest's hand: not exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן — אִין, אֵין חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the פשיטא challenge against רבי אלעזר on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's explanation that רבי יוסי's reason is חליפין ביד כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא of the משנה already states this reason explicitly, so his statement adds nothing.

steps.title: רבי יוסי might have been arguing only on רבי מאיר's terms
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that without רבי אלעזר, we might have read the משנה's clause as רבי יוסי arguing on רבי מאיר's terms, while personally exempting for a different reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: רבי יוסי was speaking to רבי מאיר according to רבי מאיר's own view. He meant: 'In my view, the animal is exempt even if the replacement is not in the כהן's hand. If you obligate him in the gifts, he will come to shear the animal and work with it. But according to your view, at least agree with me where the replacement is in the כהן's hand, because the רבנן treated one who did not acquire like one who acquired.' And רבי מאיר said to him: 'No.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אלעזר's statement is still needed. The משנה's clause could have been read as a debating argument, not as רבי יוסי's real reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this possible reading, רבי יוסי's own reason is a fear: if the owner gives gifts, he will treat the animal as fully ordinary and come to shear it or work with it (גיזה ועבודה). That reason would exempt even with no replacement. The 'replacement' argument was only a fallback offered within רבי מאיר's framework. רבי אלעזר teaches that the replacement is truly רבי יוסי's own reason.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; introduces a mistaken assumption that a statement comes to correct
According to his (the other person's) words or view
Shearing and working the animal, which are forbidden with a בכור
At least agree with me
One who did not actually acquire is treated as one who acquired

steps.confusionAlert: The 'מהו דתימא' reading is the one the גמרא rejects. In the end, רבי יוסי's real reason is that the replacement is with the כהן.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common גמרא tool. An argument made 'לדבריו', on the other side's terms, is not necessarily the speaker's own reason.

phrases.english: Lest you say:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לִדְבָרָיו דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ —
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei was speaking to him according to Rabbi Meir's words:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי, אֲפִילּוּ אֵין חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: 'In my view, it is exempt even if there is no replacement in the priest's hand,
because if you obligate him in the gifts,
he will come to shearing it and working with it;
phrases.notes: He will think the animal is ordinary and fully permitted

phrases.english: according to you, at least agree with me
where the replacement is in the priest's hand,
since they treated one who does not acquire like one who acquires;'
and Rabbi Meir said to him: 'No.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לִדְבָרָיו דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the משנה's clause could have been read differently, so the statement is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's real reason was the fear of גיזה ועבודה. The replacement argument was only addressed to רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר teaches that רבי יוסי's own reason is חליפין ביד כהן.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's statement is needed. Without it, we might think רבי יוסי's replacement argument was only a debating point against רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רב פפא: everyone agrees a doubtful tithe animal is exempt from the gifts
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that in the case of ספק מעשר, all agree there is no obligation to give the priestly gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא said: Everyone agrees that a doubtful מעשר animal is exempt from the priestly gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is brought, from רב פפא. He limits the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי so that it does not include a doubtful tithe animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute so far is about a doubtful בכור. רב פפא adds that when the doubt is whether an animal is מעשר בהמה, even רבי מאיר agrees there are no gifts. This sets up the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
An animal that may or may not be מעשר בהמה (the animal tithe)

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said:
Everyone agrees regarding a doubtful tithe animal
that it is exempt from the priestly gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement limiting the scope of the same dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספק מעשר is exempt from the priestly gifts according to all opinions, including רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Isn't רב פפא's statement obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who 'everyone' is meant to include. If it means רבי מאיר, that is obvious, because his reason applies only to a doubtful בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone agrees': who is that meant to include? רבי מאיר? That is obvious! רבי מאיר only obligated there, in the case of a doubtful בכור, because the כהן comes at the owner from two sides. But for a doubtful מעשר, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's statement as unnecessary. The point it makes about רבי מאיר seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a doubtful בכור, the כהן can claim from two sides: 'If it is a בכור, it is mine; if it is not, give me the gifts.' So רבי מאיר obligates. With a doubtful מעשר, the animal is never the כהן's, so there is no 'two sides' claim. Why would רב פפא need to tell us that רבי מאיר agrees?

keyTerms.meaning: Obvious; a challenge that a statement is unnecessary
An animal that may or may not be a firstborn
From two sides: the כהן wins either way
Only up to this point does he say; it limits someone's opinion

phrases.english: 'Everyone agrees': who is meant?
Rabbi Meir? That is obvious!

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָמְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir only obligates there
in the case of a doubtful firstborn,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וּבָא עָלָיו כֹּהֵן מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין,
phrases.english: since the priest comes at him from two sides,
phrases.notes: Either it is a בכור and the כהן takes it, or it is ordinary and the כהן takes the gifts

phrases.english: but a doubtful tithe animal: no.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״הַכֹּל מוֹדִים״ — מַאן? רַבִּי מֵאִיר? פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב פפא's statement in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's statement that all agree ספק מעשר is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's reason (the כהן comes from two sides) clearly does not apply to מעשר, so his agreement is self-evident.

steps.title: We might have thought רבי מאיר's reason is to keep the gifts from being forgotten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought רבי מאיר's reason is so that the law of the gifts is not forgotten. That reason would apply even to ספק מעשר, so רב פפא teaches otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: רבי מאיר's reason is so that the law of the gifts will not be forgotten, and then even a doubtful מעשר would also be obligated. So רב פפא teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב פפא's statement is needed. There was another possible reason for רבי מאיר that would have made him obligate even a doubtful tithe animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר's concern were general, keeping people from forgetting the practice of gifts, it would apply to any doubtful case. רב פפא shows that רבי מאיר's reason is specifically the 'two sides' claim of the כהן. That claim exists only with a doubtful בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason
So that the law of the priestly gifts will not be forgotten
He teaches us (that this is not so)

phrases.english: Lest you say:
the reason of Rabbi Meir
is so that the law of the gifts will not be forgotten,
so even a doubtful tithe animal would be obligated too?
He teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּלֹא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח תּוֹרַת מַתָּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows an alternative reason we might have assigned to רבי מאיר, which makes the statement necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר obligates so that the law of the gifts is not forgotten, which would apply to ספק מעשר too.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's reason is the כהן's two-sided claim, which applies only to ספק בכור. So ספק מעשר is exempt according to all.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר obligates gifts only for a ספק בכור, because the כהן wins 'from two sides.' A ספק מעשר is exempt according to everyone.

steps.title: Challenge from the later clause of the משנה about replacements
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the הוה אמינא from step 5. It quotes the סיפא, where רבי יוסי and רבי מאיר argue about an animal whose replacement is with the כהן. That shows their argument is tied to the כהן's claim, not to keeping the law from being forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you say that? The end of the teaching says that רבי יוסי held: any animal whose replacement is in the כהן's hands is exempt from the gifts, and רבי מאיר obligates!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion that רבי מאיר's reason is 'so the law of the gifts is not forgotten.' It does this by quoting the סיפא of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides argue specifically about an animal whose replacement (חליפין) is with the כהן. This suggests that רבי מאיר's reason depends on the כהן having a claim on the animal, which only happens with a ספק בכור. If so, nobody could ever have thought רבי מאיר obligates in ספק מעשר, and רב פפא's ruling seems unnecessary again.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really say this? (opens a challenge)
The latter clause of a teaching
Replacements; the animal given in exchange
The priestly gifts (foreleg, cheeks, and stomach)

phrases.english: And can you say this?
But doesn't the latter clause teach:
that Rabbi Yosei would say:
Any animal whose replacements are in the hand of a priest
is exempt from the gifts,
and Rabbi Meir obligates!
phrases.notes: Their argument centers on the כהן's claim, not on remembering the law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ הָכִי? וְהָקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הוה אמינא offered in step 5's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one might have thought רבי מאיר's reason was so that the law of the gifts not be forgotten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא shows the dispute is about an animal whose replacement is with the כהן. That points to a reason tied to the כהן's claim, which applies only to a ספק בכור, so there was never room to think רבי מאיר obligates in ספק מעשר.

steps.title: The dispute over replacements shows the strength of רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we could have read the סיפא differently. רבי מאיר might obligate even in ספק מעשר, and the case of replacements was chosen only to show how far רבי יוסי goes in exempting. רב פפא therefore teaches that רבי מאיר does exempt in ספק מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: רבי מאיר obligates even in ספק מעשר. They argue about replacements only to show the strength of רבי יוסי, who exempts even where the כהן has a claim from both sides. So רב פפא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the need for רב פפא's ruling. It shows that the סיפא could have been read in a way that still leaves room for the mistaken idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Choosing the case of replacements does not prove what רבי מאיר's reason is. It could have been chosen to show רבי יוסי's bold position: he exempts even when the כהן seems to win either way. The כהן owns either this animal itself or its replacement. So the הוה אמינא stands, and רב פפא's ruling is needed to reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
To show you the strength of his position
Comes at him from two sides; has a claim either way
It teaches us (the conclusion is otherwise)

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's ruling is needed after all. רבי מאיר does not obligate the gifts in ספק מעשר, even though one could have misread the משנה's clause that way.

phrases.english: Lest you say:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אֲפִילּוּ סְפֵק מַעֲשֵׂר מְחַיַּיב,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir obligates even in a case of uncertain tithe,
and the fact that they disagree about replacements
is to inform you of the strength of Rabbi Yosei,
who exempts even where
the priest comes upon him from two sides,
phrases.notes: Either this animal is the בכור, or its replacement is already with the כהן.

phrases.english: so he teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by reinterpreting why the סיפא chose the case of replacements.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the purpose of the source's case choice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר obligates even in ספק מעשר. The replacement case only shows the strength of רבי יוסי's exemption.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב פפא teaches that רבי מאיר too exempts in ספק מעשר.

steps.title: משנה: if one of the two dies, רבי טרפון says divide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה. Two male animals were born and one of them is a בכור, but we don't know which. If one of them died, רבי טרפון says the כהן and the owner divide the one that is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died, רבי טרפון says: they divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה, setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי טרפון held that the כהן takes the better of the two animals. Here, when one has died, he says to split the remaining one. The next step will ask why that makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: They divide (split the value)
Firstborn male animal, which belongs to the כהן

phrases.english: If one of them died,
Rabbi Tarfon says: They divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן, רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: יַחְלוֹקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic by quoting the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי טרפון, when one of the two dies, the כהן and the owner split the survivor.

steps.title: Why divide? Just check which one died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי טרפון says to divide. By his own earlier view, the better animal belongs to the כהן. So if the fat one died, the survivor belongs to the owner, and if the lean one died, the survivor belongs to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why should they divide? Let's look: if the fat one died, it was the כהן's, and the one left is the owner's. If the lean one died, it was the owner's, and the one left is the כהן's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי טרפון's ruling to divide, using his own earlier rule against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון earlier said the כהן takes the better one, since the healthier animal is presumed to have come out first. With that rule, there is no doubt left about who owns the survivor. So dividing seems to contradict his own reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Let us see / let us check
Fat, healthy
Lean, thin
The owner (the Israelite)

phrases.english: Why should they divide?
Let us see:
If the fat one died, it is the priest's,
and this one that remains is the owner's;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי כָּחוּשׁ מִית — דְּבַעַל הַבַּיִת מִית,
phrases.english: and if the lean one died, the owner's died,
and this one that remains is the priest's!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי יַחְלוֹקוּ? נִיחְזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just quoted in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי טרפון's ruling that they divide.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי טרפון's own rule that the better animal is the כהן's identifies the owner of the survivor, so there is no reason to divide.

steps.title: רבי טרפון changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that רבי טרפון retracted his earlier view that the כהן takes the better one. He then held that they always divide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: רבי טרפון retracted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי resolves the contradiction by saying רבי טרפון gave up his earlier rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling to divide reflects רבי טרפון's later position, not his earlier one. Once he no longer holds that the better one is the כהן's, there is real doubt about the survivor, and splitting makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted; changed his ruling

steps.confusionAlert: Both rulings still appear in the משנה, but they are not two views held at the same time. Dividing is רבי טרפון's later, final view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Rabbi Tarfon retracted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: חָזַר בּוֹ רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: the earlier ruling was abandoned
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי טרפון still holds the כהן takes the better animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי טרפון retracted and holds they divide.

steps.title: משנה: רבי עקיבא says the claimant must prove
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא's view in the משנה. Whoever wants to take something from another person must bring proof, so the survivor stays with the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: one who wants to take from his fellow must bring the proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the opposing view in the משנה, setting up רבי חייא's parable that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is in the owner's possession. The כהן is the one trying to take it, so without proof the כהן gets nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who takes from his fellow bears the burden of proof

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of monetary law that applies throughout ש״ס.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
One who takes from his fellow, the proof is upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: הַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the next clause of the משנה, the view that disagrees with רבי טרפון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner keeps the survivor unless the כהן proves it is his.

steps.title: רבי חייא's parable of the shepherd
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא explains רבי טרפון with a parable. Two people left sheep with a shepherd, and one sheep died. The shepherd places the survivor between them and walks away, so they divide it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said: what is רבי טרפון's case like? It is like two people who deposited animals with a shepherd. The shepherd puts the remaining one between them and leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא gives a comparison that explains when רבי טרפון's ruling to divide applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parable shows that רבי טרפון is discussing an animal that neither side clearly holds. With no one in possession, the rule that the claimant must prove does not decide the case, so they split it. This explains why רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא can reach different outcomes.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable or comparison
To what is the matter comparable?
They deposited (left in someone's care)
Withdraws, removes himself

steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון says divide in a case where neither side has possession. רבי עקיבא says the owner keeps the animal, because the claimant must bring proof.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya said:
The parable of Rabbi Tarfon's view:
To what is the matter comparable?
To two people who deposited animals with a shepherd,
where the shepherd places it between them and withdraws.
phrases.notes: Neither side holds the animal, so they divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא: מָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the case behind רבי טרפון's ruling, in contrast to רבי עקיבא's rule in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון's ruling applies where the animal is held by neither side, like a shepherd's deposit, so the two parties divide it.

steps.title: A parable for רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא gives a parable for רבי עקיבא's view. It is like someone who deposited an animal with a homeowner: whoever wants to take from the other must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the parable for רבי עקיבא: What is this like? It is like one person who left an animal with a homeowner. The rule there is that whoever wants to take from the other must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא already gave a parable for רבי טרפון. Now he gives a matching parable for רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A homeowner has his own sheep, and someone leaves one more sheep with him. One sheep dies, and nobody knows whose it was. The living sheep is in the homeowner's domain, so he keeps it unless the other person proves it is his. In the same way, the owner keeps the surviving animal unless the כהן brings proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable or comparison
He deposited (left something in someone's care)
A homeowner (here, one who owns his own animals)
One who wants to take from another must bring proof

phrases.english: And the parable of Rabbi Akiva:
phrases.notes: Still said by רבי חייא, continuing from Step 12.

phrases.english: To what is the matter comparable?
To one who deposited [a sheep] with a homeowner,
phrases.notes: The homeowner has sheep of his own.

phrases.english: where one who takes from his fellow must bring the proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pairs with רבי חייא's parable for רבי טרפון in Step 12, giving the opposite model.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי עקיבא's model, the surviving animal stays in the owner's domain, so the כהן must bring proof.

steps.title: If the parables are different cases, what is the argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the dispute really is. Surely רבי עקיבא would not argue with the shepherd case, and רבי טרפון would not argue with the homeowner case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what are they arguing about? Would רבי עקיבא argue about two people who left sheep with a shepherd, where the shepherd puts the sheep down and walks away? And would רבי טרפון argue about one person who left a sheep with a homeowner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the two parables. They seem to describe two different situations, so it is not clear that the two תנאים disagree at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the shepherd case, nobody owns the place where the sheep is, so splitting makes sense. In the homeowner case, the homeowner holds the sheep, so the other person needs proof. Each rule is obvious in its own case, so nobody would argue with either one. The question is: where is the real dispute?

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?
A shepherd (a neutral caretaker)
Withdraws, walks away

phrases.english: But about what do they disagree?
Does Rabbi Akiva disagree
about two who deposited [sheep] with a shepherd,
where the shepherd puts it down and walks away?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. Of course he does not disagree.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Tarfon disagree
about one who deposited [a sheep] with a homeowner?
phrases.notes: Also rhetorical. Of course he does not disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the pair of parables from Steps 12 and 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the two parables show a real dispute between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each parable's rule is obvious in its own case, and neither תנא would reject the other's. So the parables do not show where they actually disagree.

steps.title: Both agree on the parables; the dispute is a mixed case
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רב פפא) says everyone agrees on both parables. They argue only when the animals are in the owner's courtyard and the shepherd is a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say it was רב פפא: Everyone agrees that when two people left sheep with a shepherd, the shepherd puts the sheep between them and walks away. And everyone agrees that when one person left a sheep with a homeowner, whoever wants to take from the other must bring proof. They disagree only when the animals are in the homeowner's courtyard and the shepherd is a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. He admits that both parables are agreed upon, and he points to a mixed case where they argue. The next two steps explain each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real case is in between the two parables. The animals are in the owner's courtyard, which looks like the homeowner case. But the shepherd caring for them is a כהן, which gives the כהן some connection, like the shepherd case. The question is which parable this case is more like.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (it was a different אמורא)
Everyone agrees
They disagreed only in this case
A courtyard (a place that can acquire things for its owner)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two shepherds. In the parables, the shepherd is a neutral outsider. In the real case, 'רועה כהן' means the כהן himself is the shepherd caring for the owner's animals.

phrases.english: Rava said, and some say it was Rav Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בִּשְׁנַיִם שֶׁהִפְקִידוּ אֵצֶל רוֹעֶה —
phrases.english: Everyone agrees about two who deposited [sheep] with a shepherd
that the shepherd places it between them and walks away,
and about one who deposited [a sheep] with a homeowner
that one who takes from his fellow must bring the proof.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בַּחֲצַר בַּעַל הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: They disagree only [when the animals are] in the homeowner's courtyard,
and the shepherd is a Kohen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב פָּפָּא: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 14 by moving the dispute to a specific mixed case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case redefinition: both models are agreed upon, and the dispute is placed in a case between them.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each תנא seemed to reject the other's parable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both parables are agreed upon. The argument is only about the owner's courtyard when the shepherd is a כהן.

steps.title: רבי טרפון: the owner shares his courtyard for the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון holds that the owner gives the כהן a share in his courtyard so the כהן can acquire the בכור. The owner wants the מצוה done with his property, so the case is like the shepherd parable and they split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון holds: The owner transfers to the כהן a share in his courtyard, because he is happy for a מצוה to be done with his property. So this is like two people who left sheep with a shepherd, where the shepherd puts the sheep between them and walks away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי טרפון's side of the courtyard case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard normally acquires things for its owner, which would favor the owner. But רבי טרפון says the owner wants the מצוה of giving the בכור to happen, so he gives the כהן a share in the courtyard. Now both of them hold the courtyard, neither one fully has possession, and they split, just like the shepherd case.

keyTerms.meaning: He actually transfers ownership to him
He is pleased, it suits him
A commandment (here, giving the בכור to a כהן)
His property or money

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon holds:
He [the owner] transfers to him [the Kohen a share] in his courtyard,
because he is happy that a מצוה be done with his property,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ כִּשְׁנַיִם שֶׁהִפְקִידוּ אֵצֶל רוֹעֶה,
phrases.english: so it is like two who deposited [sheep] with a shepherd,
where the shepherd places it between them and walks away.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן סָבַר: אַקְנוֹיֵי קָא מַקְנֵי לֵיהּ בַּחֲצֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the dispute that Step 15 defined.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner shares his courtyard with the כהן for the sake of the מצוה. The case then matches the shepherd parable, and they divide.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the owner gives nothing because he might lose
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that the owner might lose out, so he gives the כהן no share in his courtyard. The case is like the homeowner parable, and the כהן must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא holds: Since the owner might suffer a loss, he does not give the כהן anything. So this is like one person who left a sheep with a homeowner, where whoever wants to take from the other must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי עקיבא's side of the courtyard case. This finishes רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a case of doubt, giving the כהן a share could make the owner lose an animal that may not even be a בכור. A person does not willingly give away rights when it might cost him money. So the courtyard stays fully the owner's, he keeps possession, and the כהן is the one who must bring proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
A loss
Anything

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree on the two parables: with a neutral shepherd they split, and with a homeowner the other side needs proof. They argue about the owner's courtyard when the כהן is the shepherd. רבי טרפון says the owner shares the courtyard for the מצוה, so they split. רבי עקיבא says he shares nothing because of possible loss, so the כהן must bring proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole argument depends on one question about human nature: does a person give away rights for a מצוה even when it might cost him money? The answer decides who has possession, and possession decides who must bring proof.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds:
Since he [the owner] could have a loss,
he does not transfer anything to him [the Kohen],

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ כְּאֶחָד שֶׁהִפְקִיד אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: so it is like one who deposited [a sheep] with a homeowner,
where one who takes from his fellow must bring the proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לֵיהּ פְּסֵידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side to Step 16 and completes רבא's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of possible loss, the owner gives the כהן no share in the courtyard. The case then matches the homeowner parable, and the כהן must bring proof.

steps.title: Two first-time ewes: two males, or a male and a female
steps.stepSummary: Two ewes that never gave birth before deliver two males, so both go to the כהן. If they deliver a male and a female, the male goes to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone's two ewes had never given birth and they gave birth to two males, both go to the כהן. If they gave birth to a male and a female, the male goes to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with the simplest case. Each first-time ewe gave birth, so any male born is surely its mother's first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ewe had exactly one lamb, and neither ewe ever gave birth before. So every male here is certainly a בכור, and there is no doubt at all. These clear cases set the baseline before the משנה adds doubtful cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. It marks the start of a new משנה.
Ewe / his ewes (female sheep).
That had not yet given birth for the first time.
A firstborn male animal, which is given to the כהן.

phrases.english: MISHNA
His two ewes that had not given birth before
and they gave birth to two males
both of them go to the priest.
phrases.notes: Each male is its own mother's firstborn.

phrases.english: A male and a female:
the male goes to the priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁתֵּי רְחֵילָיו שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion of the parables of רבי חייא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two first-time ewes each bear one lamb, every male is a certain בכור and goes to the כהן.

steps.title: Two males and a female: one lamb to the priest, but which one?
steps.stepSummary: With two males and a female, one male is surely a בכור and goes to the כהן. רבי טרפון says the כהן picks the better one. רבי עקיבא says they assess the lambs and the כהן gets the leaner one. The other male grazes until it gets a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two males and a female: one is his and one goes to the כהן. רבי טרפון says: the כהן chooses the nicer one. רבי עקיבא says: they assess the lambs between them. The second lamb must graze until it becomes blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: Now doubt enters. Three lambs came from two ewes, so one ewe had twins. We know one male is surely a בכור, but we cannot tell which one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ewe bore a single lamb, and the other bore twins. If the single lamb is a male, that male is surely a בכור. If the single lamb is the female, then the twin-mother bore both males, so one of them was surely born first. Either way, one male is certain, which is why the כהן gets one. רבי טרפון lets the כהן take the best. רבי עקיבא gives him only the leaner one, because he must prove any claim to more. The leftover male might be a בכור, so it cannot be used until it has a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: Chooses / selects.
The nicer, better lamb.
They assess the lambs' fatness between them. In practice the כהן takes the leaner one.
It shall graze, meaning it is left out to pasture.
Until it gets a מום (blemish), after which it may be slaughtered.

steps.confusionAlert: Both lambs are not doubtful in the same way. One male is certainly a בכור, and we just don't know which. That is why the כהן gets one for sure, and the argument is only about which one.

phrases.english: Two males and a female:
one is his and one is for the priest.
Rabbi Tarfon says:
The priest chooses for himself the better one.
Rabbi Akiva says:
They assess between them,
phrases.notes: The כהן receives the leaner lamb.

phrases.english: and the second must graze until it becomes blemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבָה אֶחָד לוֹ וְאֶחָד לַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the certain cases to the first doubtful one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One male goes to the כהן. רבי טרפון says the better one, and רבי עקיבא says the leaner one. The doubtful second male grazes until it gets a מום.

steps.title: Does the leftover lamb owe the priestly gifts?
steps.stepSummary: When the owner slaughters the leftover lamb after it gets a מום, the תנא קמא says he must give the מתנות. רבי יוסי exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he is obligated in the gifts. רבי יוסי exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now asks what happens when the owner finally slaughters the doubtful second lamb. Must he give the כהן the usual gifts from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary animal owes the מתנות: the foreleg, the jaws and the maw. The first opinion treats this lamb like any ordinary animal. רבי יוסי exempts it, but his reason only comes out in the second half of the משנה (Step 24).

keyTerms.meaning: Priestly gifts from a slaughtered animal: the זְרוֹעַ (foreleg), the לְחָיַיִם (jaws) and the קֵבָה (maw).
Obligated.
Exempts.

phrases.english: And he is obligated in the gifts,
Rabbi Yosei exempts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַיָּיב בַּמַּתָּנוֹת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי פּוֹטֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the second lamb from Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא obligates the מתנות from the doubtful lamb, and רבי יוסי exempts it.

steps.title: If one lamb died: split, or the claimant must prove
steps.stepSummary: If one of the two males died, רבי טרפון says the כהן and the owner split the survivor. רבי עקיבא says it stays with the owner unless the כהן proves his claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died, רבי טרפון says: they divide. רבי עקיבא says: whoever takes from his fellow must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new twist: one of the two males died. Now we don't know whether the survivor is the כהן's lamb or the owner's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same argument the גמרא analyzed in Steps 8–17. רבי טרפון splits the doubt between the two sides. רבי עקיבא leaves the lamb with the owner, who has possession, because the כהן is the one trying to take it.

keyTerms.meaning: One of them died.
They divide (the value).
One who wants to take from another must bring proof.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the רבי טרפון / רבי עקיבא argument about doubtful money is a general principle. It applies here exactly as it did in the earlier משנה.

phrases.english: If one of them died,
Rabbi Tarfon says: They divide,
Rabbi Akiva says:
The one who takes from his fellow bears the burden of proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר יַחְלוֹקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the two-males-and-a-female case, now with one lamb dead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון says they split the survivor. רבי עקיבא says it stays with the owner unless the כהן brings proof.

steps.title: Two females and a male, or two of each: the priest gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: If the births were two females and a male, or two males and two females, no male is surely a בכור. So the כהן cannot claim anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two females and a male, or two males and two females: the כהן has nothing here.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes the first section with cases where there is no certain בכור at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each of these cases, both ewes might have given birth to a female first. Then every male came second. Since no male is certainly a בכור, the כהן has no sure claim.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן has nothing here, meaning no certain claim.
Females.
A lamb that may or may not be a בכור.

steps.whatToRemember: First section rule: the כהן gets a lamb only if at least one male is surely a בכור. If every male could have been born second, he gets nothing.

phrases.english: Two females and a male
or two males and two females:
the priest has nothing here.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת וְזָכָר אוֹ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּשְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the set of cases with two first-time ewes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When every male could have come after a female, the כהן receives nothing.

steps.title: One ewe gave birth before, one did not: two males
steps.stepSummary: If one ewe had given birth before and the other had not, and two males were born, one goes to the כהן. The same רבי טרפון / רבי עקיבא argument applies, and the second lamb grazes until it gets a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one ewe had given birth before and one had not, and two males were born, one is his and one goes to the כהן. רבי טרפון says: the כהן chooses the nicer one. רבי עקיבא says: they assess between them, and the second grazes until it becomes blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The second half of the משנה begins with a new setup. Now only one ewe is a first-time mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ewe that never gave birth surely produced one of the two males, so one male is a certain בכור. The male from the experienced ewe is not a בכור at all. Since we cannot tell them apart, the rules are the same as in Step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: One ewe had already given birth before.
And one ewe had not given birth before.
The first to open the womb. This is what makes an animal a בכור.

phrases.english: One had given birth before, and one had not given birth before,
and they bore two males:
one is his and one is for the priest.
Rabbi Tarfon says:
The priest chooses the better one.
Rabbi Akiva says:
They assess between them,
and the second must graze until it becomes blemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַת בִּיכְּרָה וְאַחַת לֹא בִּיכְּרָה וְיָלְדָה שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a parallel set of cases, with one experienced ewe and one first-time ewe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One of the two males goes to the כהן, with the same argument over which one. The other grazes until it gets a מום.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's reason for exempting the gifts, and רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: The משנה repeats that the owner owes the מתנות, while רבי יוסי exempts. It now gives רבי יוסי's reason: an animal whose replacement is held by the כהן is exempt. רבי מאיר obligates.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he is obligated in the gifts. רבי יוסי exempts, for רבי יוסי says: any animal whose replacement is in the hand of a כהן is exempt from the gifts. And רבי מאיר obligates.
steps.whatsHappening: The gifts argument comes back, and this time the משנה explains why רבי יוסי exempts. It also names רבי מאיר as the one who obligates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner's lamb is really the בכור, then the lamb the כהן took is really the owner's ordinary lamb. So the כהן is already holding this animal's 'replacement.' רבי יוסי says that is enough to exempt the owner from giving gifts. רבי מאיר disagrees and requires the gifts anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Replacement / whose replacement.
In the כהן's possession.
Obligates.

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the short ruling of רבי יוסי back in Step 20. The same reason applies to both halves of the משנה.

phrases.english: And he is obligated in the gifts.
Rabbi Yosei exempts,
for Rabbi Yosei says:
Any animal whose replacement is in the priest's possession
is exempt from the gifts.
And Rabbi Meir obligates.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר כֹּל שֶׁחֲלִיפָיו בְּיַד כֹּהֵן פָּטוּר מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels Step 20 and adds רבי יוסי's reasoning and רבי מאיר's name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי says an animal whose replacement is held by the כהן is exempt from the מתנות. רבי מאיר obligates.

steps.title: If one died in the second case: the same argument
steps.stepSummary: Here too, if one male died, רבי טרפון says they split, and רבי עקיבא says the כהן must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died, רבי טרפון says: they divide. רבי עקיבא says: whoever takes from his fellow must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the death case for the second set of ewes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubt has the same shape as in Step 21, so the two opinions stay the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Proof.
His fellow, meaning the other party.
Money or property whose owner is in doubt.

phrases.english: If one of them died,
Rabbi Tarfon says: They divide.
Rabbi Akiva says:
The one who takes from his fellow bears the burden of proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר יַחְלוֹקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels Step 21 for the second set of ewes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון says they split, and רבי עקיבא says the כהן must bring proof.

steps.title: Male and female in the second case: the priest gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: If the experienced ewe and the first-time ewe produced a male and a female, the כהן gets nothing. The male might be from the ewe that gave birth before.
steps.simpleTranslation: A male and a female: the כהן has nothing here.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with the case where no male is surely a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The male may have come from the ewe that already gave birth, which would make him not a בכור. The female may have come from the first-time ewe. Since the male is only doubtful, the כהן has no sure claim. Compare Step 18, where the same male-and-female births went to the כהן because both ewes were first-time mothers.

keyTerms.meaning: Male.
Female.
Certain, the opposite of סָפֵק (doubtful).

steps.whatToRemember: Across the whole משנה, the כהן gets a lamb only when at least one male is certainly a בכור. When there is a certain one but we don't know which, רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא argue over which lamb he takes and what happens if one dies.
steps.confusionAlert: The births are the same as in Step 18 (a male and a female), but the result is the opposite. Here one ewe already gave birth before, so the male is no longer certainly a בכור.

phrases.english: A male and a female:
the priest has nothing here.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second set of cases and contrasts with Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With one experienced ewe, a male-and-female birth gives the כהן nothing, because the male is only a ספק בכור.

steps.title: Why the first case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says all the cases were needed. If the משנה had taught only the first case, one ewe giving birth to two males, we might think רבי עקיבא holds his view only there, because both lambs came from the same mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was necessary to teach every case. If the משנה had taught us only the first case, we would say that רבי עקיבא holds his view there because both lambs came from one mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by explaining why the משנה repeated the same argument in several cases. It starts with the first case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, one ewe gave birth to two males, and רבי עקיבא says the כהן cannot claim the better lamb. Both lambs came from the same womb, so there is no reason to think the stronger one came out first. The גמרא warns that someone might limit רבי עקיבא's view to that kind of case only.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. This opens a צריכותא, which shows why each case is needed.
It taught us.
The first case
Two from one, meaning two lambs born to one mother

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is necessary [to teach all the cases],
for if it had taught us only the first case,
phrases.notes: The first case is one ewe that gave birth to two males.

phrases.english: [I would say that] in that case Rabbi Akiva says his view,
because the two came from one [mother].
phrases.notes: Since both come from the same womb, neither has an edge.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן קַמַּיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins the גמרא's explanation of why the משנה repeated the argument between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first case alone would not prove that רבי עקיבא holds his view where the lambs come from different mothers.

steps.title: In the two-ewe case, רבי עקיבא might have agreed with רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: In the case of two first-time ewes that gave birth to two males and a female, one lamb came out alone. Since that single lamb is stronger, we might think רבי עקיבא agrees there with רבי טרפון. So the second case was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But take his two ewes that had not given birth before, where one ewe had two lambs and the other ewe had one. There I might say רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי טרפון, because the lamb from the ewe that had only one baby is stronger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the second case teaches something new. Without it, we might think רבי עקיבא gives in to רבי טרפון there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second case, one mother had twins and the other had a single baby. A lamb that grew alone in its mother is healthier, so we might reason that the כהן should get that better lamb, as רבי טרפון says. By teaching this case, the משנה shows that רבי עקיבא still disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: His ewes (female sheep)
They had given birth before, so their next babies would not be בכורות
I might say. This introduces a mistaken idea we might have had.
He agrees with him
Better or stronger

steps.confusionAlert: שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרוּ means the ewes had NOT given birth before. They are first-time mothers, so their first male IS a בכור.

phrases.english: But [in the case of] his ewes that had not given birth before,
where two came from one [ewe] and one came from the other,
I might say he agrees with Rabbi Tarfon,
because the one from the ewe that bore a single lamb is stronger.
phrases.notes: A lamb that grew alone in its mother is healthier than a twin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל רְחֵילָיו שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes the first half of the צריכותא by showing what the first case alone would leave out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second case teaches that רבי עקיבא holds his view even when one lamb was born alone and is stronger.

steps.title: Why the second case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only the second case, we might limit רבי עקיבא's view to two first-time mothers. When one ewe had given birth before and the other had not, and two males were born, we might think he agrees with רבי טרפון. The reason continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught us only this second case, I would say רבי עקיבא holds his view there because both ewes were first-time mothers. But where one ewe had given birth before, the other had not, and they had two males, I might say he agrees with רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the third case and explains why the second case alone would not cover it. The sentence is cut off here. The reason is given right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second case, both mothers were first-time mothers, so their lambs came out in similar conditions. In the third case, only one mother was a first-time mother, so only her male is a בכור. The גמרא suggests that this difference might make רבי עקיבא agree with רבי טרפון, and its explanation of why continues next.

keyTerms.meaning: She had given birth before
Both of them
Males

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only this [second case],
[I would say that] in this case Rabbi Akiva says his view,
because both had not given birth before,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַחַת בִּיכְּרָה וְאַחַת שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרָה
phrases.english: but where one had given birth before and one had not,
and they gave birth to two males,
I might say he agrees with Rabbi Tarfon,
phrases.notes: The reason is given at the start of the next passage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins the second half of the צריכותא, which shows why the third case is also needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second case alone would not show that רבי עקיבא holds his view when only one of the two ewes was a first-time mother.
